title: Shortest Path Breaking at Most K Walls
statement: You are given an m x n grid where each cell is 0 (open floor) or 1 (a wall), plus an integer k. Starting at the top-left cell (row 0, column 0) you want to reach the bottom-right cell (row m-1, column n-1). Each move steps to one of the four orthogonally adjacent cells that lies inside the grid. During the whole journey you may eliminate (walk through) at most k wall cells; entering a wall cell counts as one of your k eliminations, and the top-left or bottom-right cell being a wall also costs an elimination when you occupy it. Return the minimum number of moves needed to reach the bottom-right cell, or -1 if it cannot be reached within the elimination budget. The grid always has at least one row; a row may be empty (zero columns), in which case there is no destination and the answer is -1. If the start cell is also the destination (a 1 x 1 grid), the answer is 0 provided the elimination budget covers it.
hints: This is a shortest-path-in-an-unweighted-grid question, so exploring outward level by level gives the answer in moves — but a plain cell is no longer the full picture. What extra fact do you carry alongside (row, col)?

The state is (row, col, eliminations_remaining). Two arrivals at the same cell are genuinely different if they have different budgets left, so track the best (largest) remaining budget ever seen per cell and only re-enqueue when you arrive with strictly more budget than before.

Seed the queue with the start cell and k minus its own value (return -1 if that is negative). Each BFS level increments the step count; for every in-bounds neighbor compute nrem = rem - grid[nr][nc], skip if nrem < 0, return the current step count the moment the neighbor is the bottom-right cell, and otherwise enqueue it only if nrem beats best[nr][nc].
